context.title: Enumeration of matchings with no 2-left-nestings
context.statement: Let a matching on $[2n]$ be a set of $n$ disjoint arcs joining pairs of vertices. Assume that $i<j<k<\ell$, and call the arcs $(i,\ell)$ and $(j,k)$ **$m$-left-nesting** when $j-i\leq m$. A $1$-left-nesting is therefore an ordinary left-nesting. Let $\mathfrak{f}_n$ denote the sequence defined in the source. **The 2-left-nesting conjecture.** Among all matchings on $[2n]$, exactly $\mathfrak{f}_n$ have no $2$-left-nestings. The claim is presented as an additional conjecture in the paper's discussion of matching enumeration.
context.source_name: Anders Claesson and Svante Linusson, “n! matchings, n! posets”, arXiv:1003.4728 (2010).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.4728

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2010).

context.title: Aval's oriented tree isomorphism conjecture
context.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be trees equipped with orientations $\gamma$. For an orientation $\gamma$, let $\chi_G^\gamma(x;q)$ denote the oriented chromatic quasisymmetric function obtained by weighting proper colorings according to the number of oriented ascents. **Aval's oriented tree isomorphism conjecture.** If $G$ and $H$ are non-isomorphic oriented trees, then

$$
\chi_G^\gamma(x;q)\neq\chi_H^\gamma(x;q).
$$

This generalizes the tree isomorphism conjecture to oriented chromatic quasisymmetric functions. The supplied text gives no resolution status for this oriented version, so it remains open in this record.
context.source_name: Laura Colmenarejo and Ian Klein, “The Total Chromatic Quasisymmetric Functions of a Graph”, arXiv:2601.23170 (2026).
context.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.23170

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “Notably, Hikita's proof of the Stanley-Stembridge conjecture does not imply the Shareshian-Wachs conjecture, leaving the latter still open.”

context.title: Stones–Wanless conjecture on reduced Latin squares
context.statement:
Let $rels(n)$ and $rols(n)$ denote the numbers of reduced even and reduced odd Latin squares of order $n$, respectively. **Stones–Wanless conjecture.**

$$
rels(n)\neq rols(n)
$$

for all positive $n$. The source presents this as another extension of the Alon–Tarsi conjecture to odd orders; no resolution status is supplied for the full statement.

context.note: rels(n) != rols(n): small n agree with the claim; deciding new n needs parity counts of reduced Latin squares beyond current computation. No search run.

context.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hereditary family, let $\mu(\mathcal{H})$ denote the size of a smallest base of $\mathcal{H}$, and let $\mathcal{H}^{(r)}$ be its $r$th level. The $r$th level has the **$t$-star property** when its largest $t$-intersecting subfamilies are $t$-stars. **Holroyd–Talbot conjecture.** If $1 \leq t \leq r$ and

$$
\mu(\mathcal{H}) \geq (t+1)(r-t+1),
$$

then $\mathcal{H}^{(r)}$ has the $t$-star property. This generalizes the Holroyd–Talbot conjecture and includes the case of the power-set levels; it remains open in the stated generality.
context.title: Holroyd–Talbot conjecture for levels of hereditary families
context.reason: Power-set EKR is a special case; arbitrary hereditary bases do not give a uniform complete level. Corpus refuted reference conflicts with open statement.
context.next_lemma_or_obstruction: Read primary t-star convention (maximum attained by a star versus all maximizers stars); prove arbitrary-family bound or nontrivial exact counterexample.

context.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hereditary family, let $\mathcal{H}^{(r)}$ and $\mathcal{H}^{(s)}$ be its levels, and suppose $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{H}^{(r)}$ and $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{H}^{(s)}$ are cross-$t$-intersecting, meaning every $A\in\mathcal{A}$ and $B\in\mathcal{B}$ satisfy $|A\cap B|\geq t$. **Empty-family extremal conjecture.** If $1\leq t\leq r\leq s$ and

$$
\mu(\mathcal{H})\geq r+s-t+1,
$$

then

$$
|\mathcal{A}|+|\mathcal{B}|\leq |\mathcal{H}^{(s)}|.
$$

Equivalently, when empty families are allowed, the maximum is attained by $\mathcal{A}=\emptyset$ and $\mathcal{B}=\mathcal{H}^{(s)}$. This is presented as a strong generalization of Kamat's conjecture and remains open in the source.
context.title: The empty-family extremal conjecture for hereditary levels
context.reason: Setting A empty proves attainability but not the universal cross-t bound. Hereditary shadows are not automatically matchable at the stated threshold.
context.next_lemma_or_obstruction: Construct a weighted shadow injection at mu>=r+s-t+1, or exact cross-intersecting hereditary witnesses violating the sum.

context.literal_statement: Let $C_{0,1,1}(N)$ be the Rademacher coefficient associated with the pole at $x=1$ in the partial-fraction decomposition of the generating function for partitions into at most $N$ parts. **Oscillation conjecture.** The function $C_{0,1,1}(N)$ oscillates with “period” $32$, and its local maxima and local minima attain arbitrarily large positive and negative values, respectively, as $N$ increases. This is an empirical refinement of the paper's evidence against Rademacher's conjecture; it describes the observed behavior of one coefficient sequence and remains a conjectural, data-based statement.
context.ordinary_detail: Approximate period32 is not an exact period assertion. Need a coefficient asymptotic with nonzero oscillatory amplitude, exponential growth and a phase argument giving both signs. Observations and formal residue expansion alone do not supply error bounds. Original unread.
